question.prompt: What is the area of the region in the coordinate plane defined by the inequality \[\bigl||x| - 1\bigr| + \bigl||y| - 1\bigr| \le 1?\]

solutions.title: Find one quadrant and reflect
solutions.explanation:
Changing the sign of either coordinate leaves the inequality unchanged, so all four quadrants contribute equal areas.

Where \(x,y\ge0\), the inequality becomes
\[
|x-1|+|y-1|\le1.
\]
Divide this region along the lines \(x=1\) and \(y=1\). In the part where \(x,y\ge1\), put \(a=x-1\) and \(b=y-1\). The condition is
\[
a\ge0,\qquad b\ge0,\qquad a+b\le1.
\]
This describes the right triangle with vertices \((1,1)\), \((2,1)\), and \((1,2)\). Its perpendicular legs both have length \(1\), so its area is \(\tfrac12\).

The other three parts use the other choices of direction from \((1,1)\) and give congruent triangles. Together they form the diamond with vertices
\[
(0,1),\ (1,0),\ (2,1),\ (1,2).
\]
Its area is therefore \(4\cdot\tfrac12=2\).

Reflecting this diamond across the coordinate axes gives the entire region. The four copies have disjoint interiors, so shared boundary points do not affect the total area. The answer is
\[
\boxed{4\cdot2=8},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).

solutions.title: Take half of each unit square
solutions.explanation:
The nested absolute values behave linearly between consecutive integers, which lets us find the included area one unit square at a time.

Define \(f(t)=\bigl||t|-1\bigr|\). Since both terms in \(f(x)+f(y)\le1\) are nonnegative, each is at most \(1\). Thus \(|x|,|y|\le2\), and the whole region lies in the square \([-2,2]\times[-2,2]\).

On the four unit intervals, we have

| Interval for \(t\) | \(f(t)\) |
|---|---|
| \([-2,-1]\) | \(-t-1\) |
| \([-1,0]\) | \(t+1\) |
| \([0,1]\) | \(1-t\) |
| \([1,2]\) | \(t-1\) |

On each interval, \(f\) equals \(0\) at one endpoint and \(1\) at the other, changing at a constant rate.

The integer-coordinate grid divides the bounding square into \(4\cdot4=16\) unit squares. In each unit square, exactly one corner has \(f(x)=f(y)=0\). Let \(a,b\) be the horizontal and vertical distances from that corner. The table shows that \(f(x)=a\) and \(f(y)=b\), so the condition becomes \(a+b\le1\). This selects a right triangle with legs \(1\), exactly half of the unit square.

These squares cover the bounding square and overlap only along edges. Consequently, the total area is
\[
\boxed{16\cdot\frac12=8},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).
